[[McDonough Gymnasium]] |champion = |tourney = [[2025 College Basketball Crown|College Basketball Crown]] |tourney_result = Quarterfinals }} {{2024–25 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgetown University]] in the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hoyas, led by second-year head coach [[Ed Cooley]], were members of the [[Big East Conference]]. The Hoyas played their home games in [[Washington, D.C.]], at both [[Capital One Arena]] and [[McDonough Gymnasium]]. The team's performance was markedly better than in the previous several seasons. Georgetown finished the season with a record of 18-16 while going 8–12 in Big East play to finish the year in seventh place in the conference. This marked the Hoyas' first year with a winning record and highest finish in Big East play since the [[2018-19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2018-19 season]]. In the [[2025 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East Tournament]], the Hoyas lost to [[2024-25 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] in the first round.{{cite web|url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2025/3/12/mens-basketball-shorthanded-hoyas-fall-to-10-depaul.aspx|title=Shorthanded Hoyas Fall to #10 DePaul in Big East Tournament|date=March 12, 2025|website=guhoyas.com|access-date=July 30, 2025}} At the conclusion of the season, Georgetown was selected to play in the inaugural [[2025 College Basketball Crown|College Basketball Crown]] tournament. The Hoyas defeated [[2024-25 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]] for their first postseason victory since 2015 before ending their season with a loss to [[2024-25 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] in the second round.{{cite web|url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2025/4/3/mens-basketball-mens-basketball-falls-to-nebraska-in-college-basketball-crown-quarterfinals.aspx|title=Men's Basketball Falls to Nebraska in College Basketball Crown Quarterfinals|website=guhoyas.com|access-date=July 30, 2025}} Following the season [[Thomas Sorber]] and [[Micah Peavy]] were selected in the [[2025 NBA Draft|NBA Draft]], marking the first time that two Hoyas players were selected in the same draft since [[2008 NBA Draft|2008]].{{cite web|url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2025/6/26/mens-basketball-micah-peavy-headed-to-the-new-orleans-pelicans-with-no-40-pick-in-2025-nba-draft.aspx|title=Micah Peavy Headed to the New Orleans Pelicans with No. 40 Pick in 2025 NBA Draft|date=June 26, 2025|access-date=July 30, 2025}} ==Previous season== After cutting ties with head coach [[Patrick Ewing]] in 2023 after six years at the helm, the Hoyas played their first season under head coach [[Ed Cooley]], who had left the head coaching position at [[Big East Conference|Big East]] rival [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence College]] to come to Georgetown. Under Cooley, the Hoyas had their third historically bad season in a row in 2023–24, starting 7–4 in non-conference games but finishing the season 9–23 overall and 2–18 in Big East play. They finished in 10th place in the 11-team conference. In the [[2024 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they lost to [[2023–24 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the first round, bringing their season to an recap== ===Non-conference season=== Georgetown played 11 non-conference games between November 6 and December 28, finishing 9–2 in nonconference play.{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2024/8/27/24229863/georgetown-hoyas-release-2024-nonconference-schedule-lehigh-fairfield-notre-dame-wvu-syracuse-cooley|title=Georgetown Releases 2024 Nonconference Schedule|author=Whipple |date=27 August 2024 |website=Casual Hoya |publisher= |access-date=28 August 2024}} The non-conference schedule included the Hoyas playing in the final year of the [[Big East–Big 12 Battle]], facing former Big East rival [[2024–25 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] on the road. The Hoyas also played former Big East member [[2024–25 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] on the road in the annual renewal of their rivalry. All other non-conference games were at home, two of them on campus at [[McDonough Arena]] and the rest at [[Capital One Arena]]. Georgetown met former Big East opponent [[2024–25 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] at Capital One Arena in the second season of a two-year home-and-home series.{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2024/4/23/24138805/schedule-reports-georgetown-hears-opponent-for-final-big-east-big-12-battle-west-virginia-ed-cooley|title=SCHEDULE REPORTS: Georgetown Hears an Opponent for Final Big East-Big 12 Battle|author=Whipple |date=23 April 2024 |website=Casual Hoya |publisher= |access-date=6 May 2024}} For the second season in a row Georgetown hosted an unnamed and unsponsored multi-team event, again referred to as the "Georgetown MTE." In the 2024 Georgetown MTE, each of three participating teams played each other once, with the Hoyas hosting both [[2024–25 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]] and [[2024–25 Saint Francis Red Flash men's basketball team|Saint Francis]] and Mount St. Mary's hosting Saint Francis.{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2024/6/12/24166464/saintly-scheduling-georgetown-expected-to-host-mount-st-marys-and-st-francis-in-mte-big-east|title=SAINTLY SCHEDULING: Georgetown Expected to Host Mount St. Mary's and St. Francis in MTE|author=Whipple |date=12 June 2024 |website=Casual Hoya |publisher= |access-date=14 June 2024}} Plans for Georgetown and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] to begin a four-year home-and-home series in the 2024–25 season changed in mid-May 2024, with the beginning of the series reportedly pushed back until the [[2025–26 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2025–26 season]] and Maryland hosting the first meeting, the change blamed on scheduling difficulties in 2024–25.{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2024/5/16/24157277/links-georgetown-maryland-series-reportedly-pushed-hoyas-transfer-portal-roster-big-east-ed-cooley|title=LINKS: Georgetown-Maryland Series Reportedly Pushed a Year|author=Whipple |date=16 May 2024 |website=Casual Hoya |publisher= |access-date=16 May 2024}} In late June, the schools confirmed these plans for the series.{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2024/6/25/24185718/get-umd-next-year-georgetown-maryland-rivalry-to-reboot-in-2025-hoyas-terrapins-cooley-willard|title=GET UMD NEXT YEAR: Georgetown-Maryland Rivalry to Reboot in 2025|author=Whipple |date=25 June 2024 |website=Casual Hoya |publisher= |access-date=25 June 2024}} Georgetown finished with a record of 9–2 in non-conference play. ===Conference season=== Georgetown played a 20-game conference season from December 18 through March 8, meeting each Big East opponent in a home-and-home series. The Hoyas finished with a conference record of 8–12. ===Big East tournament=== Georgetown lost to [[2024–25 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] in the first round of the [[2025 Big East men's basketball tournament|2025 Big East tournament]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York City]] on March 12. ===National Invitation Tournament=== Georgetown received an invitation to the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament]], but was contractually obliged to decline it because of a Big East Conference commitment to participate in the inaugural [[College Basketball Crown]] tournament. ===College Basketball Crown=== Georgetown accepted a bid to the [[2025 College Basketball Crown]] tournament.
